findings.statement: Rank 1 in the convergence ranking. Strongly tumour-up in TCGA-KIRC [gene=CA9; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=9.71]. Tractable (antibody) with drugs returned by Open Targets: girentuximab (PHASE_3), radioiodine-labelled girentuximab (PHASE_2), sulthiame (PHASE_4), ethoxzolamide (WITHDRAWAL). UniProt: cell membrane / microvillus membrane, so it is accessible to antibodies and imaging. DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency [gene=CA9; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; mean_effect_ccrcc=0.051], and no fraction of ccRCC lines depends on it. This makes it a targeting-antigen and imaging/diagnostic biomarker, not a functional dependency. PRISM shows a non-significant signal from a multi-target compound, so it is uninformative.

Rank 4 in the convergence ranking. Tumour-up and tumour-intrinsic. Open Targets tractability: antibody and other clinical modalities (AB: Advanced Clinical). Drugs: vorsetuzumab (PHASE_1), vorsetuzumab mafodotin (PHASE_1), MDX-1411 (PHASE_1), cusatuzumab (PHASE_2). UniProt: plasma membrane ligand of CD27. No selective DepMap dependency [gene=CD70; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.006], so it is an antigen for ADC/CAR-T or antibody use and not a driver. Also expressed on activated lymphocytes, which is an on-target off-tumour consideration.

Rank 30 in the convergence ranking. Tumour-up and tumour-intrinsic. Open Targets lists the antibody-drug conjugate AGS-16C3F at PHASE_2. UniProt: apical cell membrane, and also secreted. This is a membrane antigen that is tractable but untested at late stage in this graph; no dependency evidence.

Established ccRCC drug target (HIF-2 alpha). Open Targets association score [gene=EPAS1; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.4871]. Belzutifan is at APPROVAL. DepMap shows modest selective dependency in ccRCC lines [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.3], with about a fifth of lines dependent, but the selectivity is not statistically significant. It is not a common essential. Rank 39 in the convergence ranking, because RNA is not strongly differential; the activity is protein/pathway-level.

Top Open Targets association with ccRCC (rank 1 in disease top targets). Recurrently mutated in ccRCC [gene=VHL; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.483]. Loss drives HIF stabilisation (the pathway behind CA9, EPAS1 and HILPDA upregulation). A tumour suppressor, so it is not directly druggable, and DepMap selectivity is negative (not a dependency).

Second-ranked Open Targets association with ccRCC, and a significant recurrent driver [gene=PBRM1; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.362]. A loss-of-function chromatin-remodelling tumour suppressor: association-only, with no direct drug. Relevant as a stratification biomarker, not a target.

Rank 8 in the convergence ranking, strong tumour-up, tumour-intrinsic and associated with worse prognosis in TCGA (survival record available). Highest biomarker-profile scores of the top genes. However ccRCC lines do not depend on it, and the mean effect is positive [gene=NNMT; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; mean_effect_ccrcc=0.316]. No drugs in Open Targets. This is a prognostic/diagnostic biomarker with a weak target case.

Rank 2 in the convergence ranking, tumour-up with strong RNA and protein change and TCGA replication. Open Targets lists ME-344 (PHASE_1_2) and metformin (WITHDRAWAL) for it, but these are mitochondrial/metabolic agents and not specific to this gene. Treat as a biomarker. Location and function not checked.

Rank 3 in the convergence ranking. Strongly down in tumour (proximal tubule marker), replicated in TCGA, and low expression tracks worse survival (significant TCGA survival record). No drugs. A diagnostic/prognostic biomarker of loss of proximal-tubule identity, not a target (down-regulated).

Rank 6 in the convergence ranking, with a genetic association in Open Targets and tumour-up, replicated in TCGA. Predicted tractable but no drugs listed in Open Targets. DepMap shows no ccRCC selectivity, so the target case is untested and weak.

caveats: Across the top-ranked candidates no ccRCC-selective CRISPR dependency was found (CA9, CD70, NNMT, SCARB1 are all non-dependent), so these are antigen/biomarker cases, not functional-dependency targets. EPAS1 is the exception, with modest selectivity that is not significant.
Only a subset of genes had STRING, UniProt and mutation checks; COXFA4L2, ALDOB and SCARB1 were not profiled for location or driver status beyond the ranking record.
PRISM is a 2D screen and misses HIF-2 biology; CA9 PRISM hit is non-significant and from a multi-target compound.
Many top biomarkers (ALDOB, SLC22A8, UMOD, FABP1) are kidney-lineage genes lost in tumour; this may reflect tissue composition, although the ranking applies a purity adjustment.
